Entries.Text: Edit the design file of the selected CharaInitParam row: the file in param/asmparam/asmparam.designbnd named by the row's assemDataID. In game, the design overrides the row's equip fields, so it sets the AC's parts, names and paint. Changes are saved with the params (or with Save Designs), and you can undo them.
This row has no design, because its assemDataID isn't set. Create one below, or point the row at an existing design.
asmparam.designbnd has no design file {0}. Some vanilla rows (such as 800 to 807) point at designs that aren't in it.
Add a design file for this row, copied from a template design. If the row has no assemDataID, it is set to the new design's ID.
The ID of the new design file, written to the row's assemDataID. Vanilla designs mostly use their row's ID, so that is suggested when free; otherwise, the next free ID after it.
The design ID must be above 0.
This ID already has a design: {0}. Pick another ID to create a new one, or link the row to this one. Edits to a shared design change every row that uses it.
Set the row's assemDataID to this design without creating a file.
Create the design file from the template, with parts taken from the row's equip fields, and set the row's assemDataID to it. One undo step reverses both.
The design to copy. Its names, paint, decals and markings are kept, and its parts are replaced with the row's equip fields.
Create the design file from the template, with parts taken from the row's equip fields.
The names stored in the design. Older designs have no Data Name.
The design's data name (the DataName section). Vanilla designs often use it as a label.
The parts in the design's Assemble section. Type an ID, or pick a row from the list. Middle-click a part to open its row in a new view.
The {0} row ID. -1 leaves the slot empty.
Pick a row. Middle-click to open this row in a new view.

Set the parts from the row's equip fields: equip_Wep_Right/Left for the arm units, equip_Bolt/Arrow for the right/left back units, equip_Helm, equip_Armer, equip_Gaunt, equip_Leg, equip_Booster_Main, equip_Fcs, equip_Generator and equip_AssaultDrive.
The Assemble values whose use is unknown, as stored. In vanilla designs, slots 12 and 13 hold the BackRail Weapon Loader rows (299300 and 299100), and 7 and 14 are empty.

The paint in the design's Coloring section: 14 records of six colours each. Which part each record paints isn't mapped yet. In vanilla designs, records 6, 7, 9 and 10 are almost always the default grey.
The record's four additional colours, at offset 48. Their meaning is unknown.
Copy this whole record (its colours and other values) over the other 13.
Write asmparam.designbnd to the project. Saving the params also does this.
AC Assembly: link row {0} to design {1}
AC Assembly: change part in design {0}
AC Assembly: fill design {0} from row
AC Assembly: change coloring of design {0}
Couldn't find {0} in the project or the game data.
